projection.title: L-shaped room
projection.prompt: A room shaped like an L is made of two rectangles: one that is 6 meters by 4 meters, and another that is 3 meters by 2 meters. What is the total area of the room?

deterministicValidator.equivalenceNotes: Accept 30 with or without a unit phrasing.

projection.accessibilityNotes: Present the two rectangles' dimensions as plain text; do not depend on a floor-plan image or color.
projection.accessibleAlternative: Read aloud or display: An L-shaped room is made from a 6 meter by 4 meter rectangle and a 3 meter by 2 meter rectangle. Find the total area of both parts together.

projection.title: Box surface area
projection.prompt: A rectangular prism is 4 cm long, 3 cm wide, and 2 cm tall. What is its total surface area?

deterministicValidator.equivalenceNotes: Accept 52 with or without a unit phrasing.

projection.accessibilityNotes: Present dimensions as plain text; do not depend on a net-diagram image or color.
projection.accessibleAlternative: Read aloud or display: A rectangular prism measures 4 centimeters by 3 centimeters by 2 centimeters. Find the total surface area by accounting for all six faces.

projection.title: Fractional-edge prism volume
projection.prompt: A rectangular prism has length 2 1/2 feet, width 1 1/2 feet, and height 4 feet. What is its volume?
projection.accessibilityNotes: State the three fractional edge lengths and multiplication in text; no 3-D rendering is required.
projection.accessibleAlternative: Read aloud or display: Multiply two and one-half feet, one and one-half feet, and four feet to find the prism's volume in cubic feet.

projection.title: Area of a plotted rectangle
projection.prompt: A rectangle has vertices at (1, 1), (6, 1), (6, 4), and (1, 4). What is the area of this rectangle?

deterministicValidator.equivalenceNotes: Accept 15 with or without a unit phrasing.

projection.accessibilityNotes: Present coordinates as plain signed-number text; do not depend on a plotted graph image or color.
projection.accessibleAlternative: Read aloud or display: A rectangle has vertices at (1, 1), (6, 1), (6, 4), and (1, 4). Use the side lengths from these coordinates to find the rectangle's area.
